purpose: Graph-based audio-to-MIDI transcription system using spectral analysis and NetworkX algorithms

components.purpose: Performs Fourier-like spectral analysis on WAV audio files
Converts spectral data into NetworkX directed graph with temporal and harmonic edges
Uses community detection to identify fundamental frequencies from harmonics
Detects note onsets using temporal flow analysis
Converts detected note events to standard MIDI file format
Coordinates all components and provides CLI interface

interfaces.name: spectral_to_graph
interfaces.description: Spectral analyzer outputs 2D numpy array consumed by graph builder

interfaces.name: graph_to_harmonic
interfaces.description: Graph builder outputs NetworkX graph consumed by harmonic analyzer
interfaces.data_format: networkx.MultiDiGraph with temporal and harmonic edges

interfaces.name: fundamentals_to_onset
interfaces.description: Harmonic analyzer outputs fundamental notes consumed by onset detector
interfaces.data_format: List[Dict] with keys: node_id, frequency, note, intensity, time_seconds, confidence
interfaces.source_verification: Recommended solution from component delta analysis

interfaces.name: graph_to_onset
interfaces.description: Graph builder outputs graph also consumed by onset detector for temporal flow analysis
interfaces.source_verification: Recommended solution from component delta analysis

interfaces.name: onsets_to_midi
interfaces.description: Onset detector outputs note events consumed by MIDI generator
interfaces.data_format: List[Dict] with keys: onset_time_seconds, duration_seconds, velocity, note_name, midi_note
interfaces.source_verification: Recommended solution from component delta analysis

interfaces.name: midi_to_filesystem
interfaces.description: MIDI generator writes output file to filesystem
interfaces.source_verification: Recommended solution from component delta analysis

interfaces.name: orchestrator_coordination
interfaces.description: Pipeline orchestrator coordinates all components in sequence
interfaces.source_verification: Recommended solution from component delta analysis

additional_requirements: File system access for reading WAV files
File system access for writing MIDI files

ports.note: CLI tool - no network ports required

additional_info.packaging: Python package with command-line entry point

performance.scaling_strategy: none (processes one file at a time)

resource_requirements.disk: minimal (only MIDI output, no intermediate files)

pipeline_stages.output: List of fundamental notes with confidence scores
Note events with timing and velocity
pipeline_stages.processing: Temporal flow analysis for onset detection

verification_notes: Based on actual source code analysis for existing components (spectral_analyzer, audio_graph_builder, harmonic_analyzer) and detailed component delta specifications for missing components (onset_detector, midi_generator, pipeline_orchestrator). All interfaces and data flows derived from integration requirements analysis.

justification.rationale: Bottom-up integration approach starting from proven spectral analysis component. Graph-based approach using NetworkX provides interpretable results and extensibility. Pipeline architecture is linear and straightforward (DAG), making it easy to understand, test, and maintain.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Machine learning approach (CNN for onset detection, RNN for note transcription)
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Requires large training datasets, less interpretable, harder to debug. Graph-based approach provides transparency into analysis decisions.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Traditional DSP approach (peak picking, pitch tracking)
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Less robust to polyphonic music, harder to separate harmonics from fundamentals. Community detection provides superior harmonic analysis.

benefits: Extensible (easy to add new edge types or analysis algorithms)
risks: Processing speed may be slower than real-time for long files
Accuracy depends on parameter tuning (thresholds, confidence levels)
Untested on highly polyphonic music (>5 simultaneous instruments)
